source.title: CASL: Concept-Aligned Sparse Latents for Interpreting Diffusion Models
source.authors: Zheng-Hao He; Guang-Zhi Xiong; Bo-Yang Wang; Sanchit Sinha; Ai-Dong Zhang

page_placements.theme: Aggregate error or splice loss can decrease without vanishing over tested widths

record.tranche_reason: Measures SAE reconstruction error across expansion ratios, which bears on whether reconstruction error decreases or remains nonzero with SAE size. It does not test the error’s linear predictability or whether errors occur on the same tokens.
record.gate_note: Table 2 directly reports SAE reconstruction MSE across expansion ratios. The paper does not regress SAE error on input activations, measure token-level error norms or overlap across SAE sizes, compare reconstruction replacement with random errors, or analyze model loss due to the error. Other editing, probing, and classifier results concern CASL’s concept-alignment task, not the claim’s dark-matter properties.
record.test_reason: The paper trains an SAE on diffusion U-Net bottleneck activations as a tool for concept alignment. Its only SAE-error result is a routine reconstruction-quality sweep of its own SAE (Table 2). That sweep is aggregate MSE on image-model tokens. It does not analyse the error's structure, predictability, per-token behaviour, functional effect or origin. So it bears on no version of the dark-matter claim, and the record's V2 'supports' label should be removed. Even read loosely, MSE roughly halves at each doubling, from 9.27 to 0.56 (×10⁻²), with no plateau. That cannot show error 'not vanishing with scale', and DAR sparsity also changes across the sweep.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that CASL yields compact, interpretable, concept-aligned sparse directions in diffusion models, and that CASL-Steer exposes their semantic effects with higher EPR than baselines. They draw no conclusion about the structure of SAE reconstruction error.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a sparse autoencoder on diffusion U-Net bottleneck activations and reports reconstruction-quality sweeps; it does not use the claim’s error-prediction or cross-size context-overlap analyses.

fits_no_version.finding: For a ReLU/L1 SAE on a DDPM++ U-Net bottleneck (CelebA-HQ), MSE falls monotonically from 9.27 to 0.56 (×10⁻²) as the expansion ratio rises from 16 to 512. Cosine similarity rises from 0.965 to 0.998 over the same range.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Aggregate SAE reconstruction error on diffusion-model activations decreases steadily with dictionary size over 16–512× expansion.

record.problems: The reconstruction-error evidence is aggregate MSE, with no uncertainty reported for these values. It cannot show per-token error predictability, whether different SAE sizes fail on the same contexts, or whether the residual affects model computation.

untested.parts: No regression of SAE error on input activations.
No per-token error norms, no cross-size prediction, no overlap of failure contexts, and no test of an error floor at scale.
No comparison of model loss or output under SAE reconstruction versus same-size random error.
No decomposition of the error into linear and nonlinear parts.
No comparison of steering or analyses with versus without the error term. CASL-Steer adds shifts to the original activation, so the error is retained implicitly and never measured.
No comparison of architectures or training objectives with respect to dark matter.

record.verdict_notes: The main text calls the expansion-ratio table 'Table 5', but it is Table 2; Table 5 is the FFHQ λsparse sweep. The appendix states scale=32, while the main text gives γsae=128 as the default. Table 2 reports no uncertainty.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a large share of the SAE error vector is a linear function of the input activation.

Only aggregate reconstruction MSE across SAE expansion ratios is reported. Per-token error-norm predictability, whether larger SAEs fail on the same contexts, and behavior at scale beyond the tested ratios are not measured.
No comparison of model loss after replacing activations with SAE reconstructions versus random errors of the same size.
No decomposition into linear and nonlinear error components, or test of their relationship to unlearned features or further dictionary learning.
No test of behavior or circuits built with SAE features with versus without the error term.
No test of whether dark matter mostly reflects SAE training artifacts, or of better architectures or end-to-end training as alternatives.

relation.reason: The paper discusses related SAE reconstruction quality; it does not use the claim that SAE errors have predictable structure or carry missing function. Using an SAE alone does not constitute using this finding.

tranche.reason: CASL uses SAEs as a tool, but does not use the dark-matter finding. Its aggregate reconstruction-quality sweep neither tests nor relies on any of V1–V6.

source_check.notes: All six values and the cited statement are accurate, but measure aggregate SAE reconstruction quality only. Section 5.4 mistakenly refers to the expansion sweep as Table 5; its actual caption is Table 2.
